changelog: Six versions in one catch-up, and almost all of it is cards. The collection went from 94 to 150, every card in the game now has real art, and every card that can be upgraded upgrades into something you play differently rather than something you pay less for. The collection 56 new cards, and they are about the deck rather than the board. Comboing, drawing, restocking, conjuring One-Shots into your hand, hauling things back out of the discard, and paying real prices for it — the axes the old set had almost nothing on. Six new verbs carry them, all working on piles the engine already had: conjure, retrieve, restock, combo costs that read what you played earlier this turn, a next-card-resolves-twice, and the risk cards that hit everything including your own. No card upgrades by getting cheaper any more. That pass is finished — the last pure "costs 1 less" upgrades are gone, and the only cards without an upgrade are the six curses, which is correct: the answer to a curse is removal, not investment. Battle Plan+ and Adrenaline+ hand you a free card. War Drums+, Blood Frenzy+ and Berserker Rage+ pay you per kill. Frenzy+ is contagious — the doubling *moves* to the nearest ally when its holder kills. Dig In+ entrenches until the unit moves. Ion Cannon+ ignores armour, which against a 3-defense boss is worth more than the +4 it used to get. Buildings get better too. The Build category is finished, and upgraded Build cards now place beside your army instead of back next to your base — a forward outpost that arrives where the fighting is. All 150 cards have art. 56 illustrations imported, 183 faces baked; nothing falls back to the canvas compositor any more. Three new commander medals landed alongside, finishing the Engineer's trio. Pile viewers Three buttons in battle: draw, discard, and exhaust. The draw pile is grouped and sorted by name — knowing *what* is still to come is information the game should give you, while knowing the *order* is the randomness the deck is built on, so that stays hidden. Discard and exhaust list every card in the order it went in, which is history rather than foreknowledge. Exhaust only appears once something has actually been exhausted. They read live instances, so a card you upgraded this run shows its upgraded name, cost and rules. Your next move asks before it commits Tapping a blue node on the expedition map used to march the column instantly. It now tells you what the node is and what to expect, and waits for Accept or Cancel. Fixes Overstrength was unusable from the hand. Load Balancing was eating a third of the damage it claims only to spread. Free cards showed full price and greyed themselves out. The upgraded rules text on all 56 new cards was printing the un-upgraded version. The raider announced itself before you could see it. Layout The button columns drop into the corners in landscape and on desktop. The pile buttons lost their borders, the deck button left battle, and the cost tags are gone. Under the hood The download grew about 30 MB, and that is the card art — 13 MB of illustrations and the baked faces built from them. 818 tests green.
